subject.title: fix(context-engine): bound deferred turn maintenance with a per-task timeout (AI-assisted)

question: After the persistence-ordering defect is repaired, should OpenClaw retain the new opt-in maintenance timeout and generic queue timeout callback as permanent contracts?
rationale: The correctness repair is mechanical, but the new public configuration and shared queue API broaden permanent product and runtime surface beyond the narrow bug fix.

options.title: Retain the opt-in contracts
options.body: Keep the config and queue callback after repairing persistence ownership and adding focused ordering and compatibility coverage.

options.title: Reuse existing lifecycle controls
options.body: Refactor around the existing compaction timeout and release-signal mechanisms to avoid introducing new public and shared surfaces.

options.title: Defer bounded maintenance
options.body: Pause this direction until context-engine cancellation and late-effect ownership are formalized as a plugin contract.

recommendation.title: Retain the opt-in contracts
recommendation.body: Keep the config and queue callback after repairing persistence ownership and adding focused ordering and compatibility coverage.

likelyOwner.reason: The available current-main history connects this person to all three central paths, making them the best available owner for the permanent config and queue API decision.
